verdict.rationale: A community report says the RCLI component is MIT-licensed, so some source is readable under an open license. The same report and another commenter say the core inference engine, MetalRT, is proprietary or commercial, so the product is only partly open. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of license terms, confirmation of which repositories (such as the runanywhere-sdks C++ core and bindings) are open-licensed, and open source for the MetalRT engine.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: FWIW this RCLI is only MIT license but their engine MetalRT is commercial.
it's better to use open source uzu than RunAnywhere's proprietary inference engine.
